findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the parent AC4 wording ('fails closed at config load') with S3/a8ea's differ-pass gate — either amend the parent AC to 'before any outbound mutation is built' or have a sibling enforce type-decision-completeness on the config-load path.
evidence: Parent AC4: '... an unmapped-non-skipped type fails closed at config load'
Parent decomposition S3: 'load-time fail-closed on undecided types'

a8ea Finding 1: 'effective_status_map is invoked LAZILY per-ticket in the differ loop, so a per-ticket gate would NOT fire before mutations. FIX: ... call it ONCE at the top of compute_outbound_mutations'
a8ea AC `test_fail_closed_fires_before_mutation_loop` — gate fires in the differ, not at config load
findings.finding: Parent AC4 requires an unmapped-non-skipped type to fail closed 'at config load'; the covering child S3/a8ea instead fires the fail-closed gate at the top of `compute_outbound_mutations` (the outbound differ pass), explicitly because config resolution is lazy per-ticket. No sibling implements a config-load-time type-decision-completeness check. The observable outcome (fail before any mutation is built) is preserved, but the parent AC's stated location ('config load') is not literally met by any child.
scenarios: An operator loads config with an undecided syncable type but never triggers an outbound reconcile pass (e.g. runs only inbound or doctor) — the parent's 'config load' framing implies the error should surface at load; a8ea only surfaces it when compute_outbound_mutations runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend parent AC4 to state the fail-closed point as 'before any outbound mutation is built' (matching a8ea), OR add invocation of `assert_type_decisions_complete` at `mapping_config.validate`/load time so an undecided type fails closed at config load as worded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a d458 acceptance test for the compacted-ticket case (STATUS events folded into a snapshot with only the final status) proving replay is skipped and the transition degrades to the pre-S6 soft-fail backstop, not an error.
evidence: Parent AC5: 'A non-allowed transition is attempted by replay ... and, failing that (or when no recorded trail survives, e.g. a compacted ticket), drifts'

Parent Approach: 'When no recorded trail survives — e.g. a compacted ticket whose STATUS events are folded into a snapshot that keeps only the final status — replay is not applicable and the failed transition degrades to the pre-S6 per-mutation soft-fail backstop'
d458 Approach step 1 derives hops via `recorded_status_hops` that 'globs `*-STATUS.json`' with no reference to snapshot/compaction
d458 ACs cover `test_replay_aborts_when_current_status_not_in_sequence` and `test_replay_skipped_when_local_id_absent` but no compaction/snapshot-only-status case
findings.finding: Parent AC5 explicitly enumerates a compacted ticket (STATUS events folded into a snapshot that keeps only the final status) as a distinct condition under which replay is inapplicable and must degrade to the pre-S6 soft-fail. The only child covering transition replay (S6/d458) derives hops purely by globbing `*-STATUS.json` files and never mentions snapshots or compaction; its degradation ACs cover 'current status not in the recorded sequence' and 'local_id absent', but not the specific compaction case where a snapshot exists yet the STATUS event trail is gone.
scenarios: A ticket whose STATUS events were compacted into a snapshot retaining only the final status hits an invalid direct transition; the glob returns no (or truncated) hops and behavior must degrade to soft-fail exactly as pre-S6.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend d458's ACs with an explicit compaction scenario: seed a snapshot that retains only the final status and no `*-STATUS.json` trail, assert `recorded_status_hops` returns empty and `replay_transition` degrades to comment-fallback/drift (result None) without raising.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a prior-art note to the Context/Approach section comparing the mapping seam and S6 transition-replay against established cross-tracker sync tools (e.g. Exalate/Unito) and standard layered-merge config libraries, stating explicitly what rebar's project-agnostic + rebar.toml-native constraint requires that off-the-shelf approaches do not satisfy.
evidence: The Context and Approach sections ground the design solely in internal rebar precedents ('docs/config.md', 'docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md', 'docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md', 'rebar-status: labels', 'EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES') and name no external prior art.

Retrieved: Exalate Docs 'Unified Workflow via Global Transitions' and community thread 'Jira Status mapping within one instance' (community.exalate.com/t/.../7907) — 'even with the correct mapping, the target status must be reachable in the local workflow from the current status' — directly mirrors the S6 direct→replay→drift concern.
Retrieved: Exalate community 'Jira Cloud — Populating a Mandatory Comment on a Workflow transition screen' — mirrors the plan's required-field/create_defaults gotcha.

Retrieved: multiple layered-config deep-merge-with-precedence libraries/docs (confmerge, @lucid-softworks/config-merge, DeepWiki config-override-hierarchy) confirm the merge model is a standard, library-backed pattern rather than a novel one.
findings.finding: The plan commits to a hand-built config-driven cross-tracker mapping seam (layered merge; map/collapse/skip/drift for unrepresentable concepts; status-transition replay) without any consideration of the well-established external prior art for this exact problem — commercial two-way tracker-sync tools (Exalate, Unito, Backbone Work Sync) that already codify status/transition/field mapping, the 'reach target status via intermediate transitions' problem the S6 replay addresses, and the mandatory-transition-field gotcha the create_defaults block addresses.
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks why rebar re-implemented a mapping/transition-replay engine that established sync tools already provide, and finds no recorded comparison.
The replay algorithm re-discovers a reachability/intermediate-transition problem Exalate already documents solutions and pitfalls for.
